gaps.why: A feeder name is how utility engineers refer to the circuit in correspondence.
gaps.how_to_collect: Request it in the utility pre-application report.
gaps.reason: National Grid publishes a feeder ID (Master_CDF) but no feeder name.

gaps.why: Charging the battery adds load; this limit can cap charging power or require upgrades.
gaps.how_to_collect: Ask the utility in a pre-application inquiry for load capacity at the service point.
gaps.reason: National Grid's MA hosting-capacity service publishes generation hosting capacity only; no load capacity.

gaps.why: The limiting criterion (thermal, voltage, protection) tells the engineer what kind of mitigation may be needed.
gaps.how_to_collect: Request it in the utility pre-application report.
gaps.reason: National Grid's MA service does not publish limiting criteria.

site_gaps.why: Sets the battery inverter voltage and the transformer, if any, between battery and switchgear.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Customer photo of the nameplate label on the main switchboard or panel (voltage, e.g. 480Y/277V, and phase/wire).
site_gaps.safety: Do not open equipment, remove covers, or climb to photograph a transformer; photograph only labels you can see from the floor.

site_gaps.why: The main breaker and service size limit how much battery power can connect without a service upgrade.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Customer photo of the main breaker handle and its rating label (e.g. 2000 A), plus the switchboard nameplate.
site_gaps.safety: Do not open equipment, remove covers, or climb to photograph a transformer; photograph only labels you can see from the floor.

site_gaps.why: The bus rating decides whether a load-side connection passes the NEC 705.12 120% rule.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Customer photo of the switchboard or panel nameplate showing the bus rating.
site_gaps.safety: Do not open equipment, remove covers, or climb to photograph a transformer; photograph only labels you can see from the floor.

site_gaps.why: The SLD shows the service, existing generation and where the battery can tie in.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Ask the customer for any existing single-line diagram (often framed in the electrical room or in past permit sets).
site_gaps.safety: Do not open equipment, remove covers, or climb to photograph a transformer; photograph only labels you can see from the floor.

site_gaps.why: Transformer size and impedance set available fault current and can limit export and charging.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Request transformer kVA, voltage ratio and impedance from the utility (pre-application or service request).

site_gaps.why: Equipment must be rated for the available fault current at the point of connection.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Request an available-fault-current letter from the utility for the service address.

site_gaps.why: An open breaker position or bus space is the cheapest place to connect the battery.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Customer photo of the main switchboard front showing breaker positions and any blank spaces (doors closed is fine).
site_gaps.safety: Do not open equipment, remove covers, or climb to photograph a transformer; photograph only labels you can see from the floor.

site_gaps.why: The meter and service point locate the interconnection and the equipment pad.
site_gaps.how_to_collect: Customer photo of the utility meter(s) and a marked-up site photo or map showing where they are.
site_gaps.safety: Do not open equipment, remove covers, or climb to photograph a transformer; photograph only labels you can see from the floor.

cautions: Hosting capacity values are utility screening estimates, not an approval or a cost estimate, and they change over time.

A value of 0 can mean the feeder is already constrained, there is an upstream limit, or it was not analyzed. It does not mean the project cannot happen: the utility may require upgrades or conditions; confirm with a pre-application inquiry.
A battery both charges (acts like load) and discharges (acts like generation); both capacities matter.
